findings.issue: The route list is duplicated between the client (app/src/main.ts:22) and the production server; they can drift, and every route add/remove touches both.
findings.suggestion: Share one module (e.g. src/routes.ts imported by both, or have the server serve the shell for any pathname and let the client render Not found).

findings.issue: The 'find default variety, fetch its Pokémon' logic is a copy of app/src/pages/pokemon.ts:20-24.
findings.suggestion: Extract a defaultPokemon(species) helper into api.ts and use it from both pages.

findings.issue: English type labels are resolved three different ways (api.ts:150 typeNames, pages/types.ts:33, pages/team.ts:54); a labeling change means finding all three.
findings.suggestion: Consolidate on one helper (e.g. typeNames or a typeLabelMap() in api.ts) used by all callers.

findings.issue: The team grid re-implements cardList (components.ts:32) inline to append remove buttons, so card markup changes must be made twice.
findings.suggestion: Extend cardList/pokemonCard with an optional per-item suffix slot, or a small listCard(card, extra) helper.

findings.issue: CardData.hidden and the .card__note style (style.css:248) exist solely for the ability page; removing Abilities leaves them dead.
findings.suggestion: Acceptable as-is; note them when removing the feature, or move the 'Hidden ability' text to the ability page's own wrapper.

findings.issue: Implicit string contract: the home page must return title 'Pokédex' for the document-title special case.
findings.suggestion: Return an explicit flag (e.g. title: null) for 'use the default title' instead.

findings.issue: typesById is rebuilt per visit by iterating every type's full Pokémon list; a future editor adding a type-dependent feature may not realize this pipeline is home-only.
findings.suggestion: Consider a shared speciesTypesById() data helper in api.ts if type-per-species data is needed elsewhere.

summary: A small, predictable vanilla TS codebase where most changes funnel through real choke points: one sprite-URL function, one card renderer, one card-from-Pokémon mapper, one cache and URL builder. The costs are the duplicated route list between client and server, a couple of helpers copied for the team feature, and no shared 'resource page' skeleton, so new sections mean a thin new file plus two route-table edits. Solidly maintainable for a team, a notch below exemplary.
